summary: Mambasa territory (Ituri) is largely state-held along the RN4, but its eastern and southern parts (Mandima secteur around Biakato, and the Lolwa section toward Komanda) have been a core ADF operating area since 2023, with recurrent massacres; there the FARDC is the main permanent force in contested zones while the ADF holds forest camps. In 2026 the ADF expanded north from the Mambasa forests into southern Haut-Uele (Suka na Mboka base between Mambasa, Wamba and Watsa), affecting the Nduye area. Mambasa town is held by police and administration with an FARDC hub. The Okapi reserve corridor (Epulu, Bandisende) and Nia-Nia secteur are state-held, with Mai-Mai Simba poacher/miner groups raiding in the forest. NOTE: this assessment could not be checked against fresh 2026 reporting for Mambasa itself (web search unavailable), so confidence is low. A review pass (2026-10-01) could not re-check these claims either (search budget exhausted, news sites egress-blocked); it found them consistent with the neighbouring Watsa, Wamba, Irumu and Bafwasende assessments.

new_entities.name: Mai-Mai Simba (Mambasa/Bafwasende)
new_entities.description: Fragmented Mai-Mai Simba groups (successors of Paul Sadala 'Morgan' and 'Manu' factions) engaged in poaching, illegal gold mining and raids in and around the Okapi Wildlife Reserve (Mambasa, Bafwasende).

zones.description: Mambasa town (cité, all neighbourhoods) and its immediate periphery (Mputu 1 & Tepe, Kilimamweza/Tobola, Kaniki/Makoko 2)
zones.evidence: Territorial seat on the RN4 with state administration, police and an FARDC presence that serves as a hub for anti-ADF operations; ADF attacks since 2023-2025 have hit villages around the territory but no capture of the town is known. Assessed state/PNC-held; not verified with fresh 2026 reporting (web research unavailable).

zones.description: Southern Mandima secteur (Biakato/Babombi, Bella/Makusa, Katanga/Makumo, Lukaya, Mahu, Alima, Lwemba/Politiki, Sayo, Teturi/Kadodo) and forest edge at Bakaeku (Bukoka/Tepe)
zones.evidence: Since ADF units pushed north from Beni into Ituri (2022-2025), the Mandima secteur along the Komanda-Mambasa and Beni-Mangina-Biakato axes has been one of the main ADF killing zones, with repeated massacres, kidnappings and displacement; the army runs operations from its positions in Biakato and along the roads while ADF hold camps in the surrounding forest. FARDC assessed as the main permanent force in a contested zone; not verified with 2026-specific reporting.

zones.description: Northern Mandima secteur between Biakato and Mambasa (Mayuano, Bango, Some, Butama 2, Zunguluka/Pekele)
zones.evidence: Villages on the RN4 / Mandima-Mambasa road south of Mambasa town, within the ADF raiding area but closer to the territorial seat and army positions; no report of ADF territorial control known. Assessed as army-dominated road corridor.

zones.description: Lolwa health zone east of Mambasa (Lolwa/Andindulu, Mabukulu/Bengasoli, Manya, Bahaha/Bandisangu, Gorofiya) toward Komanda
zones.evidence: The Mambasa-Lolwa-Komanda section of the RN4 adjoins the Irumu/Komanda ADF zone (e.g. the July 2025 Komanda church massacre) and has seen ADF ambushes and village attacks; FARDC hold positions along the road while ADF move through the forest. Assessed contested with FARDC as the main permanent force.

zones.description: Northern Mambasa secteur toward Haut-Uele (Nduye) on the ADF route north
zones.evidence: In 2026 the ADF established a base area (Suka na Mboka) in the forest between Mambasa, Wamba and Watsa and pushed into southern Haut-Uele, implying movement through northern Mambasa around Nduye; Mai-Mai Simba poacher/miner groups also operate in this part of the Okapi reserve. FARDC assumed to hold the village with ADF contesting the surroundings. ADF presence at Nduye itself is inferred from the 2026 northward expansion (no Nduye-specific report found); start date set to 2026, when the expansion into southern Haut-Uele was reported.

zones.description: Okapi Wildlife Reserve corridor on RN4 west of Mambasa (Bandisende, Epulu/Bazinga)
zones.evidence: Epulu hosts the reserve headquarters protected by ICCN rangers with FARDC support; Mai-Mai Simba groups (e.g. the 2012 Morgan attack on Epulu) have periodically raided the area for poaching and gold but do not hold the RN4 villages. Assessed as state (army-backed) control.

zones.description: Nia-Nia secteur (Nia-Nia town on RN4, Badengaido/Chrisco, Mavuvu, Kulungu, Bafwabango/Bafwambaya villages toward Bafwasende)
zones.evidence: Western Mambasa at the junction of the RN4 (Kisangani) and the road to Isiro; no known armed-group territorial control, though Mai-Mai Simba bands active in Mambasa/Bafwasende forests occasionally raid mining sites. Default state presence assumed.
